verdict: AI chip sector sold off -5-9% Oct 14-15 on AI-spending-doubt fears; DRAM/HBM pricing and hyperscaler capex fundamentals remain firmly bullish — sentiment-fundamental disconnect is the key watch.
body_md:
## Fresh Developments (Last 24-72h)

**Signal 1 — DRAM/HBM Pricing:** TrendForce's late-September release projects Q4 2026 conventional DRAM contract prices +10–15% QoQ; NAND +15–20% QoQ; PC DRAM +13–18% QoQ. HBM annual-contract mechanics buffer quarterly moves — negotiations stalled pending next-gen platform spec finalization. 2027 HBM blended ASP revised up to +121% YoY. Pricing regime remains inflationary.

**Signal 2 — HBM4 Ramp:** Micron reportedly adding 60K HBM WPM, targeting ~100K by year-end (TrendForce/ETNews, Sep 4). SK Hynix M15X fab ramping; HBM4 volume shifted from Q2→Q3 due to HBM3E demand strength. Samsung targeting ~250K WPM by end-2026 (+47% YoY). All three suppliers shipping 8-Hi HBM4 to NVIDIA in 2H. No fresh "post-2026 correction" signal in the last 72h.

**Signal 3 — Hyperscaler AI Capex:** No Q3 earnings prints yet (expected late Oct). Latest: Big 4 (AMZN/MSFT/GOOGL/META) 2026 combined capex $720–745B, up ~78% YoY. Q2 2026 combined quarterly run-rate: $171B (up from $132B in Q1). Spending is back-loaded; Evercore and BofA now model combined 2027 capex >$1T. No guide-down signal observed.

**Signal 4 — AMD MI400 / Custom ASIC:** AMD Helios rack (~$5.25M, 72 GPUs) targeting 2H 2026 shipments. OpenAI and Meta reportedly committing up to 6GW each to AMD systems; Anthropic committing 2GW (deployment 1H 2027). Google TPU 8t/8i deployed for agentic era; Amazon Trainium 3 live for Claude training. No fresh October-specific catalyst.

**Signal 5 — Optical/Photonics:** Coherent (COHR) datacenter revenue +66% YoY in FQ4; Lumentum (LITE) fully booked until early 2029, began shipping 1.6T transceivers in Q4. COHR CPO initial deliveries expected end-2026, larger ramp 2027. FCC mulling import ban on Chinese-made optical transceivers for US datacenters — proposal only, not finalized. No major October name-specific news.

**Signal 6 — Solar:** Section 232 signed Aug 6, effective Dec 4: 15% tariff + minimum import prices ($0.22/W cells, $0.38/W modules). October all-in US module cost estimate ~$0.44/W vs. prior ~$0.30/W (+47%). Module prices fell 5% QoQ but +26% YoY. FSLR navigating inventory glut + tariff headwinds. NXT order book remains robust; analyst Buy reiterated.

**Signal 7 — Watchlist: Oct 14–15 Sector Selloff:** Broad AI chip names sold off over Oct 14–15 on "AI spending doubt" sentiment. AMD confirmed -5.7% to $570.82; MRVL -8.7% (AI spend doubts + pre-earnings); MU -4.15% (GPU memory demand fears); NVDA ~-1.9% to ~$217; AVGO ~-2%; CRDO ~-7% (Open Compute Project reaction). HIVE: No Oct news — last major catalyst was Aug $350M GPU cloud deal (~$180M annualized ARR, targeting $200M by year-end). Other watchlist names (NOW, ZS, CRM, SNOW, TSLA, GDDY, NOK, AMPX, ALMU): no fresh catalysts found.

---

## Watchlist Movers

| Name | Move | Catalyst |
|------|------|----------|
| MRVL | ~-8.7% (Oct 14-15) | AI spending doubt narrative + pre-earnings pressure |
| CRDO | ~-7% (Oct 14-15) | Open Compute Project reaction; networking sector sympathy |
| AMD | -5.7% (Oct 14-15) | Sector-wide AI capex doubt; Q3 earnings pending ~Oct 28 |
| MU | -4.15% (Oct 14-15) | GPU memory demand fears; memory selloff |
| NVDA | ~-1.9% (Oct 15) | Sector sympathy; no name-specific negative catalyst |
| AVGO | ~-2% (Oct 15) | Sector sympathy |

No notable moves in COHR, LITE, CIEN, FSLR, ENPH, HIVE, NOW, ZS, CRM, SNOW, TSLA within 72h window.

---

## Context vs. Baseline

- **Capex:** $720–745B vs. baseline $600–700B — tracking **above** original forecast. Bullish vs. baseline.
- **HBM correction thesis:** Supply building but no inflection yet; 2027 pricing being revised UP — correction clock ticking but not triggered.
- **Custom ASIC:** AMD/Google/AWS commitments gaining real scale (OpenAI, Meta, Anthropic named); NVDA still dominant but share-shift on track per baseline.
- **Solar:** Section 232 adds cost pressure on importers but is a structural tailwind for US manufacturers (FSLR).
- **Stocks vs. fundamentals:** Oct 14–15 selloff is sentiment-driven; underlying DRAM pricing, HBM ASPs, and hyperscaler capex all still rising — disconnect is the key watch.

---

## Signals Flashing

| Signal | Direction | Bull/Bear |
|--------|-----------|-----------|
| DRAM/HBM pricing Q4 | +10–15% QoQ conventional; HBM 2027 +121% YoY | Bull |
| HBM4 ramp | All 3 suppliers building; correction not yet visible | Neutral |
| Hyperscaler capex | $720–745B 2026; >$1T modeled 2027 | Bull |
| Custom ASIC share-shift | AMD gaining real commitments; on track | Neutral |
| Optical (InP/CPO) | Supply-constrained; CPO emergence 2026-end | Bull |
| Solar (Section 232) | Cost pressure on importers; US-mfr tailwind | Mixed |
| AI spend sentiment | Oct 14–15 names -5–9% on spending doubts | Bear (near-term) |

---

## Most Important Development

**Oct 14–15 AI chip sector selloff** (AMD -5.7%, MRVL -8.7%, MU -4.15%, CRDO -7%) reflects renewed market anxiety over AI infrastructure spend ROI. No fundamental catalyst has changed — DRAM pricing still rising, hyperscaler capex above baseline, HBM demand intact. This is a sentiment / pre-earnings fear gap. **AMD Q3 earnings (~Oct 28) is the next major data point**: if MI400/Helios shipment guidance disappoints, the sell-off could deepen; upside surprise could sharply reverse it. MRVL and MU earnings (also late Oct/Nov) are the next read-through for AI memory and custom silicon demand.
